indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.3.2.1: Show understanding and appreciation of the interactions and interdependencies of organisms in an ecosystem
indicator.objective: Know the places where living things live (land, air, and water)

skills.description: Name the three main places where living things live
Match a living thing to its habitat
Give examples of living things found in each habitat
Give a simple reason why a living thing is found in a particular place

misconceptions: Birds live only in the air and never on land.
Fish can live on land if they are wet.
Plants are not living things, so they do not have a habitat.
Air is not a habitat because we cannot see it.

questions.stem: What are the three main places where living things live?
questions.explanation: Living things live on land, in the air, and in water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may list specific objects instead of the three main habitats.

questions.stem: Where does a fish live?
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fish live on land.

questions.stem: Where does a bird fly?
questions.explanation: Birds fly in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think birds only live on land.

questions.stem: A goat lives on...
questions.explanation: A goat lives on land.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think goats live in the air.

questions.stem: Which of these living things lives in water?
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all animals live on land.

questions.stem: Match the animal to its home: A dog lives on...
questions.explanation: A dog lives on land.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think dogs can live in water.

questions.stem: Do plants grow on land or in the air?
questions.explanation: Plants can grow on land (in soil) or in water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all plants only grow on land.

questions.stem: Name one living thing that lives in the air.
questions.explanation: Birds and insects are living things that live in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name things that cannot fly, like a dog.

questions.stem: Ama sees a fish, a bird, and a cow. Which one lives in water?
questions.explanation: The fish lives in water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think birds live in water because they drink it.

questions.stem: Is air a place where living things live?
options: Yes, birds and insects live in the air
Yes, only fish live in the air
questions.explanation: Yes, birds and insects are living things that live in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think air is not a habitat.

questions.stem: Which of these lives on land?
questions.explanation: A goat lives on land.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse land and water animals.

questions.stem: Where does a whale live?
hints: It is a very large animal in the sea.
questions.explanation: A whale lives in water (the sea or ocean).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think whales live on land because they breathe air.

questions.stem: Why does a fish live in water?
options: It needs water to swim and breathe
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water because it needs it to swim and breathe.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fish live in water just because they like it.

questions.stem: Why do birds fly in the air?
options: To move from place to place and find food
Because they are afraid of land
hints: Where do they find their food?
questions.explanation: Birds fly in the air to move around and find food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think birds only fly to hide.

questions.stem: Kwame says 'All living things live on land.' Is he correct?
options: No, some live in water and air
No, all living things live in water
questions.explanation: No, living things live on land, in water, and in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think land is the only habitat.

questions.stem: A fish is taken out of water. Why will it die?
hints: Where does a fish get air?
It does not have lungs like us.
questions.explanation: A fish needs water to breathe. Out of water, it cannot breathe and will die.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fish can breathe air on land.

questions.stem: Name two living things that live on land.
hints: Think of animals you see on the ground.
Think of plants in the garden.
questions.explanation: Many living things live on land, such as goats, dogs, trees, and people.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name fish or birds.

questions.stem: Why can't a fish live on land?
options: It has no legs and needs water to breathe
It does not like the sun
questions.explanation: A fish cannot live on land because it has no legs to walk and needs water to breathe.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect the body parts of the fish to its habitat.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a place where living things live?
hints: Which one is dangerous and hot?
Can living things survive in it?
questions.explanation: Living things do not live in fire. They live on land, in water, and in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fire is a habitat because it exists in the environment.

questions.stem: A bird has wings. How does this help it live in the air?
hints: How does a bird move in the air?
questions.explanation: Wings help a bird to fly, which allows it to live in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think wings are for swimming.
